DesktopPet.​FormPet
Form
public
DesktopPet.​FormPet

Form2 is the main class (form) of the pet.  An ImageList will contains all images and a Timer will move the pet after a defined interval.  The animations of this form is loaded from an XML.

Variables
AnimationStep
int AnimationStep

Current step in the animation-frames list.

Every animation has a defined quantity of steps. They are calculated from: - Quantity of frames - Repeat count and repeat from If an animation has 10 different frames and frame 5 to 9 are repeated 8 times, the total of steps is 10 + 5 * 8 = 50 steps.  Once the last step was reached, the next animation will be started. If now animation is set, the SPAWN will be executed.

CurrentAnimation
TAnimation CurrentAnimation

Structure with all informations about the current animation.

hwndWindow
IntPtr hwndWindow

Handle to the current window. If this value is 0, the sheep is NOT walking on a window.

hwndFullscreenWindow
IntPtr hwndFullscreenWindow

Handle to the full screen window. If this value is 0, there is no full screen window.

currentWindowSize

IsMovingLeft
bool IsMovingLeft

If sheep is walking to left  (default).

The original eSheep was a Japanese application. So it was normal to see something from right to left.  To leave the same characteristic, moveLeft is set to true. But it doesn't matter, because the sprite and movements gives the direction...

IsDragging
bool IsDragging

IsLeaving

If the pet is leaving the screen

OffsetY
double OffsetY

Offset Y - Sprite size is taken and not the single image. So, over the taskbar or over the windows, the pet could be 1-2 pixels over the border if you didn't drawn it on the bottom of the sprite frame.  With this offset, you can re-place the pet or you can give them an offset so that it is positioned over the window (for example if you want to show a girl sitting over the taskbar, you need this function)

PositionX
double PositionX

Current X position of the form. Because an offset can be used, this is the origin of the sprite (not like Form2.Left) before an offset was interpolated with the form position.

PositionY
double PositionY

Current Y position of the form. Because an offset can be used, this is the origin of the sprite (not like Form2.Top) before an offset was interpolated with the form position.

TossForce
Vector2 TossForce

The force in which the user tossed the sheep with. Uses Vector2 for easy magnitude calculation.

IsTossing
bool IsTossing

If the pet is in tossing mode (it was tossed and is now falling).

tossVertVel
double tossVertVel

The current vertical velocity while in tossing mode.

CreateParams
protected override CreateParams CreateParams {
get
}

With this overridden function, it is possible to remove the application from the ALT-TAB list.  This, because it is not nice to see 10 times the same sheep when you press ALT-TAB (with 10 sheeps walking on your screen).  If this form is a child, remove the possibility to interact with this form.  See: https://​msdn​.microsoft​.com​/en-us​/library​/windows​/desktop​/ff700543(v=vs.85).aspx

Kill
public void Kill()

If application is closed, all forms have still 1 second to show something (change animation).

Kill, Sync, Drag, Fall, Toss, "Fall Soft" and "Fall Hard" are "Key-names" in the XML file. If you use one of them, this program will automatically run the animation linked to this names.

Sync
public void Sync()

If user press the CANCEL button in the about box, all pets are synchronized executing the SYNC-animation.

Kill, Sync, Drag, Fall, Toss, "Fall Soft" and "Fall Hard" are "Key-names" in the XML file. If you use one of them, this program will automatically run the animation linked to this names.

Timer1_Tick
private void Timer1_Tick(
object 
sender,
EventArgs 
e
)

Timer tick. The entire animation is droved through this timer. The interval is set in the XML animation file.

On each tick, the next step is called. If it fails an error message will be show and the animation will stop.

NextStep
private void NextStep()

The most important function. Each movement step is managed by this function: Will calculate how much and where a pet should be positioned in the next step.  This function is called from Timer1_Tick(object, EventArgs).
